pointers.sentence: `FETCH_ONE`, the default, fetches the value for the one instance, as before; `FETCH_PEERS` fetches it for the instance's **peers**, the instances of its model that the same run of the queryset made from the same columns and that are still alive, weakly referenced by the list they share, `ModelState.peers`; `FETCH_RAISE` raises `FieldFetchBlocked`, a `FieldError` (`django/db/models/fetch_modes.py`).

`QuerySet.fetch_mode` sets a mode on a clone, which hands it to the instances it makes from rows through a keyword 6.1 added to `Model.from_db`, `fetch_mode=None` (`django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet.fetch_mode`, `django/db/models/base.py:Model.from_db`).

Under the mode, the first read fetched all four reporters' papers in one statement (`django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py:ForwardManyToOneDescriptor.fetch_many`).
The notes liken `FETCH_PEERS` to "an on-demand `prefetch_related()`" that needs no list of fields, and mean `FETCH_RAISE` to prevent "unintentional queries" (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).
The notes of 6.1.2, not yet released at this commit, list as fixed a bug of 6.1: `FETCH_PEERS` did not batch the instances `select_related` loaded (`docs/releases/6.1.2.txt`).
At this commit each `RelatedPopulator`, which makes the instances of one joined relation, keeps its own list of peers (`django/db/models/query.py:RelatedPopulator`).

The 6.1.1 notes say that a model whose own `from_db` takes no fetch mode crashed in 6.1 when its queryset was iterated, and that 6.1.1 made it work again, though deprecated (`docs/releases/6.1.1.txt`).

At this commit `_get_from_db` inspects the override before the loop and, where it takes neither the keyword fetch_mode nor arbitrary keywords, warns and has it called without the mode, so its instances keep the default mode (`django/db/models/query.py:_get_from_db`).
`QuerySet.select_related` with no arguments leaves the relations to the compiler, which follows those that cannot be null (`django/db/models/query_utils.py:select_related_descend`).
It warns through `warn_about_external_use`, so not for Django's own calls (`django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet.select_related`, `django/utils/deprecation.py:warn_about_external_use`).

6.1 added the warning (`django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet.values_list`).
Both calls are to raise `TypeError` in Django 2028 (`docs/internals/deprecation.txt`; [What still warns: the deprecations and the releases that end them](deprecations.md)).

Since 6.1 they read the mark that call leaves, `Query.default_ordering` turned off, and take the queryset as it stands (`django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet.first`; [`get`, `first`, `count` and the other methods that run a query at once](../querysets/results.md#an-ordering-cleared-on-purpose)).
Since 6.1 it has its model's default: `QuerySet._combinator_query` switches the combined query's default back on (`django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet._combinator_query`).
The 6.1 notes give the consequence: where `values` or `values_list` has not selected a field of the ordering, the combined queryset raises `DatabaseError` (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`):

The error is Django's, so every backend raises it: `SQLCompiler.get_order_by` cannot add the ordering's column to parts whose columns `values` fixed (`django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLCompiler.get_order_by`).

The parts were cleared first because on SQLite the compiler refuses a part that keeps an ordering, its model's default included (`django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLCompiler.get_combinator_sql`; [Combining querysets: the operators and `union`](../querysets/combining.md#what-the-compiler-asks-of-the-backend)).

Since 5.2 the columns of `QuerySet.values` and `values_list` stand in the order the names were given, where the 5.2 notes say "a set of counterintuitive rules" had made combining such querysets unpredictable (`docs/releases/5.2.txt`).

`Query.set_values` records the names in `Query.selected`, from which `SQLCompiler.get_select` writes the select list (`django/db/models/sql/query.py:Query.set_values`, `django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLCompiler.get_select`).
